Note::is_digit¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::is_digit() const

Test Whether Every Character In A Cell Is A Digit¶

is_digit() reports, for each cell, whether the cell is non-empty and every byte is an ASCII digit 0–9. Use it to gate a numeric parse — a cell that passes can be turned into an integer without surprises (no sign, no decimal point, no thousands separator, no whitespace).

The check is byte-level, so it accepts only 0–9: a leading -, a ., a ,, or a Unicode digit all fail the cell. An empty cell is 0, consistent with the rest of the is_* family.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"123", "007", "12.5", "-3", "1 2", "", "12a"});
const auto mask = n.is_digit();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]

Only "123" and "007" are pure digit runs.

See Also¶

  • Note::is_alnum: letters or digits.

  • Note::contains_any_digit: “has at least one digit” rather than “is all digits”.

  • Note::RegexAccessor::match: a whole-cell pattern check for richer numeric shapes (-?\d+(\.\d+)?).
